Files (formerly Files UWP) is a free and open-source file manager application for Windows. It is known for its modern design, extensive features, and active community development.
It is built with WinUI 3 and the Windows App SDK development framework, and a large consumer of Win32 and WinRT APIs. It is also built using the MVVM app architecture.
Features
Files provides a wide range of features, including:
* Modern UI: A modern, Fluent UI-style user interface built with the WinUI framework.
* Tabbed browsing: Users can easily navigate multiple folders and files simultaneously.
* Dual-pane view: Enables side-by-side comparison and management of files and folders.
* File tags: Consumers can organize files and folders with color-coded tags.
* Extensive customization: Files comes with customizable themes, keyboard shortcuts, and other settings.
* Rich file previews: Users can view images, videos, and other files directly within the application.
* Cloud integration: Files integrates with various cloud providers, including OneDrive, Google Drive, iCloud, Dropbox, and others.

History
The Files app began in 2018 as a personal project by developer Luke Blevins. He wanted to create a "stable, open-source foundation for innovation in the file management space''," specifically for the Windows operating system.
Another developer, Yair, joined the project in 2020. Eventually, Luke left the project to Yair and he continued to build it himself alongside a growing team.
The app was ported from UWP to the Windows App SDK, allowing for the use of a more modern technology and the removal of the full trust process. It has had multiple significant milestones including a major design refresh and over three variations of the logo over time. It has seen great change over the years, initially starting off with Fluent 1 design language styles until v2 was introduced.
The app was originally free on the Microsoft Store, however was made paid by the lead developer as an experiment that he decided to keep.

Community
The Files app is an open-source project developed and maintained by a community of contributors. It was initially created by Luke Blevins in 2018 and has since grown significantly under the leadership of Yair and other developers.
Reception
The Files app has received positive reviews from users and technology publications, praised for its features, performance, and user experience. It has over 35 thousand stars on GitHub.
In 2022 Files won the Microsoft Store App Awards in the file management category, alongside Rufus. It was also included in the 2023 Microsoft Store App Awards as a runner up.
The app was entered into the UWP Community Launch event in 2020 and launched on the Microsoft Store promptly.
